description: The American Samoa Geospatial Portal is the territory's open data hub, owned and maintained by the American Samoa Department of Commerce and built with the University of Hawaii and the Pacific Islands Climate Adaptation Science Center, with contributions from the American Samoa Environmental Protection Agency and the American Samoa Power Authority. The portal read on 2026-09-28 states its goal of being a single open access location for all of American Samoa's geospatial data, and its search service lists 24 datasets, among them Tutuila flood zones, landslide risk, building footprints for Tutuila, Pago Pago harbour facilities and buoys, fuel and boat transport, cruise ship and cannery operations, gas stations, the cell sites of the territorial telecom authority ASTCA, wetlands, villages, counties and the exclusive economic zone. Coverage is American Samoa. Licence: not stated (the portal items read carry no licence: licenseInfo empty, license "none"). Access is free of charge. Caveats: layers come from different projects and dates, and power and water networks are not among the public layers. It supports hazard exposure studies of buildings, the port, fuel supply and telecom sites on Tutuila. Related record: data-usgs-pedestrian-tsunami-evacuation-time-maps-us-coasts covers tsunami evacuation for the same islands.
